name: zeotropic_hp_propane_isobutane
title: Zeotropic propane/isobutane heat pump with glide-matching sectioned exchangers (TESPy)
summary: Water-to-water heat pump on a propane/isobutane mixture (CoolProp mixture backend): superheat over the dew point, subcooling under the bubble point, and an internal pinch imposed on 50-section condenser and evaporator profiles; COP, volumetric heating capacity and condenser glide versus composition.

authors: Francesco Witte (TESPy lead developer) and the TESPy contributors
origin.course: TESPy how-to 'Zeotropic mixtures in a heat pump' (commit 19425523)

verification.summary: The TESPy model (notebook class) was re-run in a throw-away venv with the CoolProp HEOS back end: COP, heating capacity per volume, glide and both pressures agree at 0, 30, 50 and 100 % propane to <= 1.9e-9 relative. The thermopack (Peng-Robinson) sweep of the notebook, reproduced exactly, differs by <= 0.95 % (COP) and 0.35 K (glide).
verification.reference: TESPy ZeotropicHeatPumpModel of docs/how_to_guides/zeotropic_heat_pump.ipynb (commit 19425523), CoolProp HEOS mixture (0, 0.3, 0.5, 1 propane mole fraction) and thermopack engine (11 compositions, notebook stored values reproduced)
verification.notes: Same CoolProp equation of state on both sides (8.0.0 in the venv, 8.1.0dev in CoolSolve). Without the bubble/dew points as extra section boundaries the condenser pressure differs by 0.5 % (TESPy adds them, see README). Thermopack deviations are an equation-of-state effect, comparable to the thermopack-REFPROP deviations the notebook reports.

history.action: added (T-TRANSLATE of the TESPy zeotropic heat-pump how-to, card C-445)
